arxiv-2103-05692.title: Quantifying Sufficient Randomness for Causal Inference
arxiv-2103-05692.creator: Brian Knaeble, Braxton Osting, Placede Tshiaba
arxiv-2103-05692.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Brian Knaeble, Braxton Osting, Placede Tshiaba. Spurious association arises from covariance between propensity for the treatment and individual risk for the outcome. For sensitivity analysis with stochastic counterfactuals we introduce a methodology to characterize uncertainty in causal inference from natural experiments and quasi-experiments. Our sensitivity parameters are standardized measures of variation in propensity and individual risk, and one minus their geometric mean is an intuitive measure of randomness in the data generating process.

arxiv-2203-01075.title: Reliable validation of Reinforcement Learning Benchmarks
arxiv-2203-01075.creator: Matthias Müller-Brockhausen, Aske Plaat, Mike Preuss
arxiv-2203-01075.description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning (RL) is one of the most dynamic research areas in Game AI and AI as a whole, and a wide variety of games are used as its prominent test problems. However, it is subject to the replicability crisis that currently affects most algorithmic AI research. Benchmarking in Reinforcement Learning could be improved through verifiable results.

arxiv-2206-04222.title: Plasmonic gain in current biased tilted Dirac nodes
arxiv-2206-04222.creator: Sang Hyun Park, Michael Sammon, Eugene Mele, Tony Low
arxiv-2206-04222.description: Abstract Surface plasmons, which allow extreme confinement of light, suffer from high intrinsic electronic losses. It has been shown that stimulated emission of electrons can transfer energy to plasmons and compensate for the high intrinsic losses. To-date, these realizations have relied on introducing an external gain media coupled to the surface plasmon.

arxiv-2402-15792.title: Adjusting exceptional points using saturable nonlinearities
arxiv-2402-15792.creator: Qingxin Gu, Chunlei Qu, Yongping Zhang
arxiv-2402-15792.description: Abstract We study the impact of saturable nonlinearity on the presence and location of exceptional points in a non-Hermitian dimer system. The inclusion of the saturable nonlinearity leads to the emergence of multiple eigenvalues, exceeding the typical two found in the linear counterpart.

arxiv-2408-16153.title: Statistical comparison of quality attributes: a range-based approach
arxiv-2408-16153.creator: Gerhard Gössler, Vera Hofer, Hans Manner, Walter Goessler
arxiv-2408-16153.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gerhard Gössler, Vera Hofer, Hans Manner, Walter Goessler. A novel approach for comparing quality attributes of different products when there is considerable product-related variability is proposed. In such a case, the whole range of possible realizations must be considered. Looking, for example, at the respective information published by agencies like the EMA or the FDA, one can see that commonly accepted tests together with the proper statistical framework are not yet available.

arxiv-2502-00544.title: Global well-posedness and relaxation limit for relaxed compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations in bounded domain Thanks: Yuxi Hu, Department of Mathematics, China University of Mining and Technology, Beijing, 100083, P.R. China, yxhu86@163.com Xiaoning Zhao, Department of Mathematics, China Uni
arxiv-2502-00544.creator: Yuxi Hu and Xiaoning Zhao
arxiv-2502-00544.description: Abstract . This paper investigates an initial boundary value problem for the relaxed one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations. By transforming the system into Lagrangian coordinates, the resulting formulation exhibits a uniform characteristic boundary structure. We first construct an approximate system with non-characteristic boundaries and establish its local well-posedness by verifying the maximal nonnegative boundary conditions.

arxiv-2509-16892.title: Learning from Gene Names, Expression Values and Images : Contrastive Masked Text-Image Pretraining for Spatial Transcriptomics Representation Learning
arxiv-2509-16892.creator: Jiahe Qian, Yaoyu Fang, Ziqiao Weng, Xinkun Wang, Lee A. Cooper, Bo Zhou
arxiv-2509-16892.description: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics aims to connect high-resolution histology images with spatially resolved gene expression. To achieve better performance on downstream tasks such as gene expression prediction, large-scale pre-training is required to obtain generalisable representations that can bridge histology and transcriptomics across tissues, protocols, and laboratories.

arxiv-2510-14812.title: Efficient Dynamic Structured Sparse Training with Learned Shuffles
arxiv-2510-14812.creator: Abhishek Tyagi Arjun Iyer Liam Young William H. Renninger Christopher Kanan Yuhao Zhu
arxiv-2510-14812.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Abhishek Tyagi Arjun Iyer Liam Young William H. Renninger Christopher Kanan Yuhao Zhu. Structured sparsity accelerates training and inference on modern GPUs, yet it still trails unstructured dynamic sparse training (DST) in accuracy. The shortfall stems from a loss of expressivity : whereas a dense layer can realise every possible mask obtained by choosing any w w active weights out of n n , a fixed block, or N : M N{:}M layout explores only a subset of those possibilities.

arxiv-2512-20862.creator: Z. Zajicek, I. Paulescu, P. Reiss, R. M. Abedin, K. Sun, S. J. Singh, A. A. Haghighirad, A. I. Coldea
arxiv-2512-20862.description: Abstract Electronic scattering is a powerful tool to identify underlying changes in electronic behavior and incipient electronic and magnetic orders. The nematic and magnetic phases are strongly intertwined under applied pressure in FeSe, however, the additional isoelectronic substitution of sulphur offers an elegant way to separate them.

arxiv-2601-13081.title: What’s it like to be a chat? On the co-simulation of artificial minds in human-AI conversations
arxiv-2601-13081.creator: Geoff Keeling, Winnie Street
arxiv-2601-13081.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) can simulate person-like things which at least appear to have stable behavioural and psychological dispositions. Call these things characters . Are characters minded and psychologically continuous entities with mental states like beliefs, desires and intentions? Illusionists about characters say No.

arxiv-2601-18435.title: The Quantum Cliff: A Critical Proton Tunneling Threshold Determines Clinical Severity in RPE65-Mediated Retinal Disease
arxiv-2601-18435.creator: Biraja Ghoshal, xxx xxx, xxx xxx, Second Author, Third Author, & xxx xxx
arxiv-2601-18435.description: Abstract 1 Institute of Ophthalmology, University College London, London, UK. 2 Medical School, University College London, London, UK. ∗ Correspondence: b.ghoshal@ucl.ac.uk Abstract Predicting clinical severity from genotype remains a fundamental challenge in molecular medicine, particularly for enzymes whose function depends on sub-atomic-scale geometry.

arxiv-2602-02479.title: Motivation, Attention, and Visual Platform Design: How Moral Contagions Spread on TikTok and Instagram in the 2024 United States Presidential Election
arxiv-2602-02479.creator: Ni Annie Yuan, Ho-Chun Herbert Chang
arxiv-2602-02479.description: Abstract Visual social media platforms have become primary venues for political discourse, yet we know little about how moralization operates differently across platforms and topics. Analyzing 2,027,595 TikToks and 1,126,972 Instagram posts during the 2024 US presidential election, we demonstrate that issues are not necessarily inherently moralized, but a product of audience demographics, platform architecture, and partisan framing.

pmc-10545266.title: 3D Printing and Surgical Simulation for Management of Large and Giant Congenital Melanocytic Nevi
pmc-10545266.creator: Santana S. Solomon, Thomas J. Sitzman
pmc-10545266.description: Summary:Tissue expansion with subsequent adjacent tissue transfer is often the preferred and sometimes the only option for reconstruction of large and giant congenital melanocytic nevi. Successful reconstruction with maximal efficiency and optimal aesthetic outcome requires careful planning of the tissue transfer, which itself requires careful selection of the tissue expander size and positioning.

pmc-10596954.title: 7.F. Workshop: Local physical activity policy evaluation: state of the art, tools and methods and future directions
pmc-10596954.creator: Organised by: University of Limerick (Ireland), French Society of Public Health (France), Chair persons: Aurélie Van Hoye (Ireland)
pmc-10596954.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Insufficient physical activity (PA) is one of the most significant risk factors for chronic diseases and premature mortality worldwide. Public policies are recognized as upstream factors providing system change beyond individual changes. Policies have been recognised as an effective way to increase population PA levels, as they support the development of evidence-based interventions and programs in different domains, that help create a ‘healthy’ PA environment and enhanced PA opportunities.

pmc-10655679.title: Long-term prognostic value of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin-I in patients with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy
pmc-10655679.creator: Yongchao Wang, Xiaolin Wang, Yulin Yang, Hao Xu, Jian Li
pmc-10655679.description: Our objective was to evaluate the long-term prognostic value of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin-I (hs-cTn-I) in idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). First, patients were divided into an end-event group (n = 55) and a non-end-event group (n = 67). Then, patients were included in the subgroup analysis to compare the diagnostic value of brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) and hs-cTn-I in different populations.

pmc-11357231.title: Gluten Is Not Gluten
pmc-11357231.creator: Majlinda Xhaferaj, Katharina Anne Scherf, Ruggiero Francavilla
pmc-11357231.description: Wheat gluten is responsible for the unique baking properties of wheat flour, but it also causes wheat-related disorders in predisposed individuals. Different commercially available gluten materials are commonly used for a variety of assays, but a detailed characterization of their composition is missing in many cases.

Their versatility lies in their ability to conjugate with functional molecules on their surfaces and encapsulate small molecules, making them suitable for diverse applications. Gallic acid is a potent antioxidant compound that has garnered considerable interest in recent years.

pmc-12525705.creator: Andrés M. Treviño-Alvarez, Tomás Cabeza de Baca, Emma J. Stinson, Hannah T. Fry, Marci E. Gluck, Douglas C. Chang, Paolo Piaggi, Jonathan Krakoff

Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) is a hormone secreted by the liver with a putative role in energy expenditure, energy intake, and weight regulation.

pmc-12643793.title: Current Understanding of Carotid Body Paraganglioma Management
pmc-12643793.creator: Young-Wook Kim
pmc-12643793.description: Carotid body paraganglioma (CBP) is a rare neuroendocrine tumor that typically develop at the carotid bifurcation. Although most CBPs are non-functional and slow growing, some pose a risk of local invasion and distant metastasis. Advances in genetic testing have revealed that up to 50% of paragangliomas (PGLs) are linked to germline mutations, most commonly in the succinate dehydrogenase (SDHx) genes.

pmc-12653532.title: Causal Intervention and Counterfactual Reasoning for Multimodal Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
pmc-12653532.creator: Xinyu Han, Huosheng Xu, Gurmail Singh, Stéfano Frizzo Stefenon
pmc-12653532.description: Pedestrian trajectory prediction is crucial for autonomous systems navigating human-populated environments. However, existing methods face fundamental challenges including spurious correlations induced by confounding social environments, passive uncertainty modeling that limits prediction diversity, and bias coupling during feature interaction that contaminates trajectory representations.

pmc-12723323.title: Light‐Mediated Supramolecular Functionalization of Polymerization‐Induced Self‐Assembled Micelles
pmc-12723323.creator: Ruggero Rossi, Miriam Abad, Luis Oriol, Daniele Martella, Camilla Parmeggiani, Milagros Piñol
pmc-12723323.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Precise, remote control of polymeric nanoparticles via external stimuli is a key aim for the next‐generation drug delivery. As a versatile, one‐pot method, polymerization‐induced self‐assembly (PISA) produces dispersions of block‐copolymer micelles at high solids content with tunable core–corona architectures. Light is an ideal trigger to control the uptake and delivery of specific molecules inside such micelles since it can be localized, and easily tuned in intensity and wavelength.

pmc-13543825.title: Oxidative eustress is associated with AMPK and AKT activation, GLUT4 translocation and glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and fibres
pmc-13543825.creator: Eva Martín-Prieto, Leonardo A. Catalano-Iniesta, Escarlata Fernández-Puente, Jesús Palomero
pmc-13543825.description: Objectives: Reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) act as signalling molecules under physiological conditions; however, how oxidative eustress regulates glucose uptake in skeletal muscle remains poorly defined. We investigated the role of moderate oxidation in skeletal muscle glucose uptake, focusing on AKT/AMPK phosphorylation, GLUT4 translocation and functional glucose uptake.

pmc-13551347.title: Pernicious Anemia: A Rare Case of Vitamin B12 Deficiency With Hyperpigmentation and Pancytopenia
pmc-13551347.creator: Emmanuel Jojo Aryee, Helen Agyei-Yeboah, Semonti Nandi
pmc-13551347.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The clinical mimicry of vitamin B12 deficiency can often delay its recognition and treatment. Pernicious anemia remains among its major clinical causes. We report the case of a 32‐year‐old male who presented with symptoms of progressive darkened skin, fatigue, general weakness, and neurological symptoms, with examination notable of severe conjunctival pallor and prominent hyperpigmentation of the buccal mucosa, hands, and feet. Investigations revealed pancytopenia with critically low serum vitamin B12.

pmc-13650235.title: The Microbial and Chemical Terroir of Agarwood in French Guiana
pmc-13650235.creator: Kenji Maurice, Nicolas Baldovini, Alba Zaremski, Jérémie Damay, Romain Lehnebach, Yannick Estevez, Marc Ducousso
pmc-13650235.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Agarwood is a highly valued aromatic resinous wood formed in Aquilaria species following stress or infection, yet the putative microbial drivers of its quality remain poorly understood, particularly outside its native range. In this study, we investigated the bacterial and fungal communities associated with agarwood produced from Aquilaria crassna Pierre ex Lecomte planted in French Guiana and examined their relationships with volatile chemical compounds relevant to agarwood fragrance.
